item.name: Hashirama Cells
entries: These cultivated cells originate from Hashirama Senju, the legendary shinobi whose vitality and Wood Release were beyond ordinary human limits. Implanting them into a creature's body grants extraordinary regenerative power, but the cells may overwhelm an incompatible host.

entries.name: Cellular Rejection
entries: When these cells are implanted, you must succeed on a DC 17 Constitution saving throw or suffer rejection. On a failure, you take 6d6 necrotic damage, gain 1d4 levels of exhaustion, and the cells die, losing all their properties. The dead cells cannot be revived or restored. To gain the benefits of Hashirama Cells, you must obtain a new viable sample and undergo the implantation procedure again.

entries.name: Cellular Regeneration
entries: At the start of each of your turns during combat, if you have at least 1 hit point, you regain hit points equal to your character level + your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1 hit point).
Outside of combat, if you have at least 1 hit point, you regain hit points equal to your proficiency bonus every 10 minutes.
If you have 0 hit points but are not dead, your cells continue to regenerate. You regain hit points equal to your proficiency bonus every 10 minutes. This regeneration stops if you die.

entries.name: Cellular Vitality
entries: Your hit point maximum increases by an amount equal to twice your character level when you receive these cells. Whenever you gain a level, your hit point maximum increases by an additional 2 hit points.

entries.name: Undying Cell
entries: Your body is exceptionally resilient against death. You gain expertise in death saving throws, meaning you add twice your proficiency bonus to death saving throws.

entries.name: Wood Release
entries: The power of Hashirama's cells grants you the ability to cast certain spells. You learn the spells listed below when you reach the specified character level. You can cast each spell once without expending a spell slot, and you regain the ability to do so when you finish a long rest. You do not need material components when casting these spells through this trait.

items: Character level 1: {@spell Druidcraft}
Character level 2: {@spell Goodberry}
Character level 3: {@spell Spike Growth}
Character level 5: {@spell Plant Growth}
Character level 7: {@spell Grasping Vine}
Character level 9: {@spell Tree Stride}
Character level 11: {@spell Wall of Thorns}
Character level 13: {@spell Regenerate}
Character level 15: {@spell Clone}
Character level 17: {@spell Imprisonment}

item.name: Sharingan
entries: The Sharingan is a powerful ocular ability belonging to the Uchiha bloodline. Its abilities develop through combat and significant experiences, allowing the wielder to awaken increasingly powerful stages of the eye.

entries.name: Sharingan Ability Modifier
entries: Constitution is the primary ability score for all ocular abilities. You use your Constitution modifier, proficiency bonus, and combined Eye Mastery Bonus to determine the attack bonus and saving throw DC of your ocular abilities, including abilities granted by advanced evolutions of the Sharingan.

entries.name: Eye Mastery Bonus
entries: Each eligible awakened eye grants an Eye Mastery Bonus based on its evolution stage. Add the bonuses from your left and right eyes together, even if they have different evolution stages.

entries.name: Ocular Attack Bonus
entries: When an ocular ability requires an attack roll, use the following modifier:

entries.text: Ocular Attack Bonus = your proficiency bonus + your Constitution modifier + your total Eye Mastery Bonus

entries.name: Ocular Save DC
entries: When an ocular ability requires a saving throw, use the following DC:

entries.text: Ocular Save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Constitution modifier + your total Eye Mastery Bonus

entries.name: Ocular Limit
entries: A creature can benefit from the Eye Mastery Bonus of no more than two eyes at a time. Only eyes installed in the creature's natural eye sockets, consisting of the left and right eye, can grant this bonus.
Additional eyes implanted elsewhere on the body, such as on the arms, forehead, palms, or chest, do not grant an Eye Mastery Bonus.
If a creature possesses more than two eligible eyes, it must choose which two eyes grant its Eye Mastery Bonus. This choice cannot be changed during combat.
Eyes that do not grant an Eye Mastery Bonus may still retain other properties and abilities granted by their respective items, unless otherwise specified.

entries.name: Copy Spell
entries: Your ocular abilities allow you to observe, analyze, and memorize spells cast by other creatures. When you can see a creature casting a spell within your line of sight, you can memorize that spell without using an action or reaction.
You can memorize spells of levels 1 through the maximum spell level determined by your ocular evolution. Cantrips cannot be copied.

You can memorize a number of spells equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum of one spell). If you attempt to memorize a spell while at your maximum capacity, you must forget one previously memorized spell before memorizing the new one.
You can cast a memorized spell without expending a spell slot. You can cast only one copied spell at a time. Once you cast a copied spell, it is removed from your memorized spells.

When you witness a creature casting a spell, you can choose to cast that spell immediately or memorize it for later use. If you choose to cast it immediately, you must cast the spell you are currently observing. You cannot immediately cast a spell that you previously memorized.

You use your Ocular Attack Bonus and Ocular Save DC whenever a copied spell requires a spell attack roll or saving throw. You must still provide any required components and meet the spell's other requirements.

entries.caption: Copy Spell
rows: Once per Short or Long Rest
Once per Short or Long Rest, or once per Initiative for each battle

entries: When you have multiple eyes with different ocular evolutions, use the highest evolution among your eligible eyes to determine your maximum spell level and usage frequency. Possessing multiple eyes does not grant additional uses.

entries.name: Taijutsu Copy
entries: Your Sharingan allows you to observe, analyze, and replicate the physical features and abilities of other creatures. When you can see a creature within your line of sight, you can attempt to copy one of its features.

entries.name: Copy Features
entries: When attempting to copy a creature's feature, you must make a Constitution saving throw. The DC equals the creature's Challenge Rating (CR). If the creature has no Challenge Rating, use its character level instead.

On a successful saving throw, you successfully analyze and memorize the chosen feature. On a failed saving throw, the attempt fails and you cannot copy that feature from the same creature again until you finish a long rest.

You can memorize a number of copied features equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum of one feature). If you attempt to memorize a feature while at maximum capacity, you must forget one previously memorized feature before memorizing the new one.
You can use a memorized feature as if it were your own, following its original rules and requirements, unless otherwise specified.

entries.name: Copy Limitations
entries: You must meet all prerequisites and requirements of a copied feature, including ability score requirements, equipment, resources, and other conditions.
You cannot copy features that require a unique biological structure, bloodline, special organ, or supernatural power source that you do not possess.
The DM determines whether a feature can be copied and whether its effects can function with your own body and abilities.

entries.name: One-Tomoe Sharingan
entries: Your Sharingan awakens in its initial form, granting you the following benefits:

items: You gain darkvision out to a range of 60 feet. If you already have darkvision, its range increases by 30 feet instead.
You have advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight.
You can discern fine visual details and follow subtle movements with supernatural precision. You have advantage on the first attack roll you make against a creature during each of your turns.

entries: Your Sharingan evolves when you experience significant events during combat. It can advance directly to a higher stage without awakening the previous stages, depending on the event that occurs.
When you defeat a hostile creature while at least one allied creature you can see is bloodied, your Sharingan advances to the Two-Tomoe Sharingan.

entries.name: Two-Tomoe Sharingan
entries: Your Sharingan develops a second tomoe, improving your ability to perceive and predict movement.
You retain the benefits of the One-Tomoe Sharingan and gain the following additional benefits:
You have advantage on initiative rolls.
You have advantage on saving throws against being charmed or against spells and other effects that create illusions.
When an allied creature you can see is reduced to 0 hit points, your Sharingan advances to the Three-Tomoe Sharingan.

entries.name: Three-Tomoe Sharingan
entries: Your Sharingan reaches its fully developed form, granting you exceptional perception and the ability to anticipate your opponents' movements.
You retain the benefits of the One-Tomoe and Two-Tomoe Sharingan.
You can cast {@spell suggestion} without expending a spell slot. Once you cast the spell in this way, you can't do so again until you finish a short or long rest.

When a creature you can see makes its first attack roll against you during each round of combat, that attack roll has disadvantage. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a short or long rest.
When an allied creature you can see dies, your Sharingan advances to the Mangekyō Sharingan.

entries.name: Mangekyō Sharingan Awakening
entries: When your Sharingan evolves into the Mangekyō Sharingan, roll 1d4 on the following table to determine the abilities awakened in your left and right eyes.

item.name: Mangekyō Sharingan : Kagutsuchi
entries: The Mangekyō Sharingan is an advanced form of the Sharingan, granting its wielder powerful ocular abilities at the cost of the eyes' durability. Its powers include enhanced perception, powerful genjutsu, reality-altering techniques, and Susanoo.

entries.name: Sharingan Energy and Durability
entries: Your left and right eyes each have a maximum Sharingan Durability equal to 10 times your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1).
Your maximum Sharingan Energy is equal to half the sum of your left and right maximum Sharingan Durability, rounded down.
When you finish a short rest, you regain Sharingan Energy equal to 20 percent of your maximum Sharingan Energy, rounded down.
When you finish a long rest, you regain Sharingan Energy equal to your maximum Sharingan Energy.

Whenever an ability reduces your Sharingan Durability, reduce the Durability of the eye used to activate that ability. If an ability specifically states that it reduces the Durability of both eyes, reduce the Durability of both your left and right eyes by the specified amount.

Your Sharingan Durability can't be restored by resting or other ordinary means. Once either eye's Sharingan Durability is depleted, that eye must be replaced with another Mangekyō Sharingan eye through transplantation.

entries.name: Enhanced Sharingan
entries: You can discern fine visual details and follow subtle movements with supernatural precision. You gain the following benefits:
You gain darkvision out to a range of 120 feet. If you already have darkvision, its range increases by 60 feet instead.
You have advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight.
You have advantage on the first attack roll you make against a creature during each of your turns.
You have advantage on initiative rolls.
You have advantage on saving throws against being charmed and against spells and other effects that create illusions.
You can cast {@spell suggestion} without expending a spell slot at will.
When a creature you can see makes its first attack roll against you during each round of combat, that attack roll has disadvantage.

entries.name: Enhanced Visual Perception
entries: At the start of your turn, you can expend 3 Sharingan Energy and reduce the Sharingan Durability of both your left and right eyes by 1 to heighten your visual perception until the start of your next turn. For the duration, you have advantage on all attack rolls you make and all saving throws you make, and attack rolls against you have disadvantage.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a short or long rest.

entries.name: Izanagi
entries: As a reaction, you can use Izanagi to alter the outcome of an event affecting yourself, treating an unfavorable outcome as an illusion and rewriting reality in your favor.

After using Izanagi, the eye used to activate this ability becomes permanently blind, and its Sharingan Durability is reduced to 0. This blindness can't be removed by resting or ordinary healing. The eye must be replaced through transplantation to restore vision.

entries.name: Izanami
entries: As a reaction, you can use Izanami to trap a creature in a repeating sequence of events, forcing it to experience a loop until it accepts the truth underlying the illusion.

After using Izanami, the eye used to activate this ability becomes permanently blind, and its Sharingan Durability is reduced to 0. This blindness can't be removed by resting or ordinary healing. The eye must be replaced through transplantation to restore vision.

entries.name: Tailed Beast Genjutsu
entries: You can expend 10 Sharingan Energy to attempt to control a creature of the Beast or Monstrosity type that you can see. The target must make a Wisdom saving throw against your feature save DC. On a failed save, the target must obey your commands while the genjutsu remains active.
Whenever you take damage, the affected creature can repeat the Wisdom saving throw, ending the effect on itself on a success.
The genjutsu ends if your Sharingan Energy is depleted.

entries.name: Skeletal Susanoo
entries: You can activate Skeletal Susanoo at any time by expending 10 Sharingan Energy and reducing the Sharingan Durability of both your left and right eyes by 2. You don't need to pay the maintenance cost on the turn you activate it. Starting at the beginning of your next turn, you can expend 10 Sharingan Energy and reduce the Sharingan Durability of both your left and right eyes by 2 to maintain it.
When you activate this Susanoo, you gain temporary hit points equal to 10 times your proficiency bonus.
While this Susanoo is active, you gain the following benefits:

items: You gain a +5 bonus to AC.
You gain a +2 bonus to all saving throws.
You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls.
The save DC of your features and spells increases by 1.
At the start of each of your turns while this Susanoo is active, you gain temporary hit points equal to 10 times your proficiency bonus, replacing any temporary hit points you currently have.

entries: You can end Skeletal Susanoo at any time, requiring no action. If you can't pay the Sharingan Energy or Sharingan Durability cost to maintain it, the form ends automatically.

entries.name: Armored Susanoo
entries: You can activate Armored Susanoo at any time by expending 25 Sharingan Energy and reducing the Sharingan Durability of both your left and right eyes by 5. You don't need to pay the maintenance cost on the turn you activate it. Starting at the beginning of your next turn, you can expend 15 Sharingan Energy and reduce the Sharingan Durability of both your left and right eyes by 3 to maintain it.
When you transform into Armored Susanoo, you gain temporary hit points equal to 25 times your proficiency bonus.
While this Susanoo is active, you gain the following benefits:

items: You gain a +10 bonus to AC.
You gain a +5 bonus to all saving throws.
You gain a +3 bonus to attack rolls.
The save DC of your features and spells increases by 3.
At the start of each of your turns while this Susanoo is active, you gain temporary hit points equal to 25 times your proficiency bonus, replacing any temporary hit points you currently have.

entries: You can end Armored Susanoo at any time, requiring no action. When you end Armored Susanoo, you revert to Skeletal Susanoo if you can still maintain it; otherwise, Susanoo ends. If you can't pay the Sharingan Energy or Sharingan Durability cost to maintain Armored Susanoo, the form ends automatically.

entries.name: Mangekyō Sharingan
entries: Each Mangekyō Sharingan awakens unique ocular abilities known as Signature Abilities. These powers embody the wielder's unique visual prowess, granting extraordinary control over flames, space, time perception, and the minds of others. Each ability is tied to a specific eye and may carry a terrible cost.

entries.name: Amaterasu
entries: As a action, You expend 15 Sharingan Energy and reduce the Sharingan Durability of the eye used by 5 to unleash the black flames of Amaterasu upon a target you can see. The target is engulfed in black flames and immediately takes fire damage equal to a number of d12s equal to your proficiency bonus.

At the start of each of the target's turns, the target takes fire damage from Amaterasu, and the damage increases by 1d12 after each instance of damage. The black flames do not extinguish themselves, and this effect continues until the target dies, you extinguish the flames, or the target escapes them using an appropriate ability.
A creature can end the effect on itself by severing or removing the body part engulfed in the flames, if physically possible. The DM determines the consequences of doing so.

A creature can also escape the flames by using a teleportation ability, such as {@spell misty step}, to move away from them. The effect ends on that creature, but the flames remain where they were left.
Resistance to fire damage does not extinguish the black flames or end this effect. Immunity to fire damage instead grants resistance to the fire damage dealt by Amaterasu.

entries.name: Kagutsuchi
entries: Kagutsuchi grants you control over the black flames of Amaterasu, allowing you to shape, manipulate, and weaponize them with extraordinary precision. You gain the following abilities:

entries.name: Black Flame Infusion
entries: You can use your bonus action to expend 25 Sharingan Energy and reduce the Sharingan Durability of both your left and right eyes by 5 to unleash the black flames of Amaterasu.

The next time you deal damage to a creature with a weapon, spell, or other feature, you infuse your attack with the black flames. The target takes additional fire damage from Amaterasu as if it had been hit by Amaterasu directly. This damage uses the damage progression described in the Amaterasu feature. The infusion ends after dealing this additional damage.

If black flames created by Amaterasu are already burning within your line of sight, regardless of their source, you can instead use this feature by expending 10 Sharingan Energy and reducing the Sharingan Durability of the eye used by 5.

entries.name: Black Flame Armor
entries: When you are hit by a melee attack, you can use your reaction to expend 25 Sharingan Energy and reduce the Sharingan Durability of both your left and right eyes by 5 to engulf yourself in the black flames of Amaterasu.
The attacker takes fire damage from Amaterasu as if it had been hit by Amaterasu directly. This damage uses the damage progression described in the Amaterasu feature.

If black flames created by Amaterasu are already burning within your line of sight, regardless of their source, you can instead use this feature by expending 10 Sharingan Energy and reducing the Sharingan Durability of the eye used by 5.

entries.name: Control Black Flame
entries: If black flames created by Amaterasu are burning within your line of sight, regardless of their source, you can use a bonus action to expend 10 Sharingan Energy and reduce the Sharingan Durability of the eye used by 5 to control and manipulate those flames. You can move or reshape the existing flames without needing to create them again.

When you move the flames onto a creature, make a ranged spell attack against that creature . On a hit, the creature is engulfed in the black flames and takes fire damage from Amaterasu as if it had been hit by Amaterasu directly. This damage uses the damage progression described in the Amaterasu feature.

entries.name: Transplantation
entries: You can attempt to replace a blinded Mangekyō Sharingan eye with another Mangekyō Sharingan eye. The transplantation requires a successful DC 20 Constitution saving throw.
On a success, the transplantation succeeds. On a failure, the transplanted eye becomes permanently blind and can't be used.

entries.name: Tsukuyomi
entries: Tsukuyomi traps a target within a powerful illusion that distorts its perception of time and reality, allowing you to inflict profound psychological torment within moments.

As a action, You expend 15 Sharingan Energy and reduce the Sharingan Durability of the eye used by 5 to make the target a Wisdom saving throw against your feature save DC. If the target makes eye contact with you while within a 30-foot-long, 5-foot-wide line extending from you, it makes this saving throw with disadvantage. On a failed save, the target is stunned and takes psychic damage equal to a number of d8s equal to your proficiency bonus. On a successful save, the target takes half as much damage and isn't stunned.

At the end of each of its turns, a stunned target can repeat the Wisdom saving throw, ending the stunned condition on itself on a success. On a failure, the target remains stunned and continues to suffer the torment of Tsukuyomi, taking psychic damage equal to a number of d8s equal to your proficiency bonus.

Once the target succeeds on this saving throw and ends the stunned condition, it must immediately make another Intelligence saving throw against your feature save DC. On a failed save, the target is frightened of you and takes psychic damage equal to a number of d6s equal to your proficiency bonus. On a successful save, the target takes half as much damage and isn't frightened.

At the end of each of its turns while frightened by Tsukuyomi, the target can repeat the Intelligence saving throw, ending the frightened condition on itself on a success. On a failure, the target remains frightened and continues to suffer the torment of Tsukuyomi, taking psychic damage equal to a number of d6s equal to your proficiency bonus.

entries: You can attempt to replace a blinded Mangekyō Sharingan eye with another Mangekyō Sharingan eye. The transplantation requires a successful DC 20 Constitution saving throw.
On a success, the transplantation succeeds. On a failure, the transplanted eye becomes permanently blind and can't be used.

entries.name: Skeletal Susanoo
entries: You can activate Skeletal Susanoo at any time by expending 10 Sharingan Energy and reducing the Sharingan Durability of both your left and right eyes by 2. You don't need to pay the maintenance cost on the turn you activate it. Starting at the beginning of your next turn, you can expend 10 Sharingan Energy and reduce the Sharingan Durability of both your left and right eyes by 2 to maintain it.
When you activate this Susanoo, you gain temporary hit points equal to 10 times your proficiency bonus.
While this Susanoo is active, you gain the following benefits:

items: You gain a +5 bonus to AC.
You gain a +2 bonus to all saving throws.
You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls.
The save DC of your features and spells increases by 1.
At the start of each of your turns while this Susanoo is active, you gain temporary hit points equal to 10 times your proficiency bonus, replacing any temporary hit points you currently have.

entries: You can end Skeletal Susanoo at any time, requiring no action. If you can't pay the Sharingan Energy or Sharingan Durability cost to maintain it, the form ends automatically.

entries.name: Armored Susanoo
entries: You can activate Armored Susanoo at any time by expending 25 Sharingan Energy and reducing the Sharingan Durability of both your left and right eyes by 5. You don't need to pay the maintenance cost on the turn you activate it. Starting at the beginning of your next turn, you can expend 15 Sharingan Energy and reduce the Sharingan Durability of both your left and right eyes by 3 to maintain it.
When you transform into Armored Susanoo, you gain temporary hit points equal to 25 times your proficiency bonus.
While this Susanoo is active, you gain the following benefits:

items: You gain a +10 bonus to AC.
You gain a +5 bonus to all saving throws.
You gain a +3 bonus to attack rolls.
The save DC of your features and spells increases by 3.
At the start of each of your turns while this Susanoo is active, you gain temporary hit points equal to 25 times your proficiency bonus, replacing any temporary hit points you currently have.

entries: You can end Armored Susanoo at any time, requiring no action. When you end Armored Susanoo, you revert to Skeletal Susanoo if you can still maintain it; otherwise, Susanoo ends. If you can't pay the Sharingan Energy or Sharingan Durability cost to maintain Armored Susanoo, the form ends automatically.

entries.name: Mangekyō Sharingan
entries: Each Mangekyō Sharingan awakens unique ocular abilities known as Signature Abilities. These powers embody the wielder's unique visual prowess, granting extraordinary control over flames, space, time perception, and the minds of others. Each ability is tied to a specific eye and may carry a terrible cost.

entries.name: Kamui
entries: Kamui grants you the power to manipulate space and dimensions, allowing you to phase through attacks, teleport across space, and pull creatures into a separate dimension. You gain the following abilities:

entries.name: Intangibility
entries: When you are targeted by an attack or an effect that would deal damage or impose an effect on you, you can use your reaction to expend 10 Sharingan Energy and reduce the Sharingan Durability of the eye used by 3 to phase your body into the Kamui dimension. The triggering attack or effect passes through you harmlessly, causing you to take no damage and suffer none of its effects.

After using this feature, you remain intangible until the end of your next turn, or until you use an action to make an attack, cast a spell, or interact with an object or creature. If you do so, your intangibility immediately ends.

While intangible, you can move through walls, floors, ceilings, objects, and creatures as if they were not there. You cannot end your movement inside an object or creature. If you would end your turn inside an object or creature, you are immediately shunted to the nearest unoccupied space and take force damage equal to 1d10 for every 5 feet you are moved.

entries.name: Teleportation
entries: You can use a bonus action to expend 5 Sharingan Energy and reduce the Sharingan Durability of the eye used by 1 to teleport yourself and any creatures of your choice within 5 feet of you to an unoccupied space you can see.

entries.name: Kamui Dimension
entries: You can use an action to expend 15 Sharingan Energy and reduce the Sharingan Durability of the eye used by 5 to create a spatial distortion at a point you can see within range. The distortion forms a 20-foot-radius sphere centered on that point.

Each creature within the sphere must make a Strength saving throw against your feature save DC. On a failed save, the creature is pulled toward the center of the sphere and takes force damage equal to a number of d10s equal to your proficiency bonus. On a successful save, the creature remains in its current space and takes half as much damage.

When a creature is pulled into the center of the sphere, it must also make a Constitution saving throw against your feature save DC. On a failed save, it takes force damage equal to a number of d12s equal to your proficiency bonus and becomes restrained. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage and isn't restrained.

The area within the sphere is difficult terrain. At the start of each creature's turn while it is within the sphere, it must make a Strength saving throw against your feature save DC. On a failed save, the creature is pulled toward the center of the sphere and takes force damage equal to a number of d10s equal to your proficiency bonus. On a successful save, the creature remains in its current space and takes half as much damage.

When a creature is at the center of the sphere, it must also make a Constitution saving throw against your feature save DC at the start of its turn. On a failed save, it takes force damage equal to a number of d12s equal to your proficiency bonus and becomes restrained. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage and isn't restrained.
A creature restrained by this feature can repeat the Constitution saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the restrained condition on itself on a success.

You must maintain concentration on the spatial distortion as if concentrating on a spell. While maintaining this concentration, you must keep your gaze fixed on the spatial distortion and cannot look away from it.

At the start of each of your turns while the spatial distortion remains active, you must expend 5 Sharingan Energy and reduce the Sharingan Durability of the eye used by 5 to sustain it. If you cannot pay this cost, the spatial distortion immediately ends.

entries.name: Transplantation
entries: You can attempt to replace a blinded Mangekyō Sharingan eye with another Mangekyō Sharingan eye. The transplantation requires a successful DC 20 Constitution saving throw.
On a success, the transplantation succeeds. On a failure, the transplanted eye becomes permanently blind and can't be used.

item.name: Mangekyō Sharingan : Kotoamatsukami
entries: The Mangekyō Sharingan is an advanced form of the Sharingan, granting its wielder powerful ocular abilities at the cost of the eyes' durability. Its powers include enhanced perception, powerful genjutsu, reality-altering techniques, and Susanoo.

entries.name: Sharingan Energy and Durability
entries: Your left and right eyes each have a maximum Sharingan Durability equal to 10 times your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1).
Your maximum Sharingan Energy is equal to half the sum of your left and right maximum Sharingan Durability, rounded down.
When you finish a short rest, you regain Sharingan Energy equal to 20 percent of your maximum Sharingan Energy, rounded down.
When you finish a long rest, you regain Sharingan Energy equal to your maximum Sharingan Energy.

Whenever an ability reduces your Sharingan Durability, reduce the Durability of the eye used to activate that ability. If an ability specifically states that it reduces the Durability of both eyes, reduce the Durability of both your left and right eyes by the specified amount.

Your Sharingan Durability can't be restored by resting or other ordinary means. Once either eye's Sharingan Durability is depleted, that eye must be replaced with another Mangekyō Sharingan eye through transplantation.

entries.name: Enhanced Sharingan
entries: You can discern fine visual details and follow subtle movements with supernatural precision. You gain the following benefits:
You gain darkvision out to a range of 120 feet. If you already have darkvision, its range increases by 60 feet instead.
You have advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight.
You have advantage on the first attack roll you make against a creature during each of your turns.
You have advantage on initiative rolls.
You have advantage on saving throws against being charmed and against spells and other effects that create illusions.
You can cast {@spell suggestion} without expending a spell slot at will.
When a creature you can see makes its first attack roll against you during each round of combat, that attack roll has disadvantage.

entries.name: Enhanced Visual Perception
entries: At the start of your turn, you can expend 3 Sharingan Energy and reduce the Sharingan Durability of both your left and right eyes by 1 to heighten your visual perception until the start of your next turn. For the duration, you have advantage on all attack rolls you make and all saving throws you make, and attack rolls against you have disadvantage.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a short or long rest.

entries.name: Izanagi
entries: As a reaction, you can use Izanagi to alter the outcome of an event affecting yourself, treating an unfavorable outcome as an illusion and rewriting reality in your favor.

After using Izanagi, the eye used to activate this ability becomes permanently blind, and its Sharingan Durability is reduced to 0. This blindness can't be removed by resting or ordinary healing. The eye must be replaced through transplantation to restore vision.

entries.name: Izanami
entries: As a reaction, you can use Izanami to trap a creature in a repeating sequence of events, forcing it to experience a loop until it accepts the truth underlying the illusion.

After using Izanami, the eye used to activate this ability becomes permanently blind, and its Sharingan Durability is reduced to 0. This blindness can't be removed by resting or ordinary healing. The eye must be replaced through transplantation to restore vision.

entries.name: Tailed Beast Genjutsu
entries: You can expend 10 Sharingan Energy to attempt to control a creature of the Beast or Monstrosity type that you can see. The target must make a Wisdom saving throw against your feature save DC. On a failed save, the target must obey your commands while the genjutsu remains active.
Whenever you take damage, the affected creature can repeat the Wisdom saving throw, ending the effect on itself on a success.
The genjutsu ends if your Sharingan Energy is depleted.

entries.name: Kotoamatsukami
entries: Kotoamatsukami is an extraordinarily subtle genjutsu that alters a target's thoughts, decisions, and will without the target realizing that its mind has been manipulated. You gain the following abilities:

entries.name: Genjutsu
entries: You can attempt to control a creature you can see with a powerful genjutsu by expending 15 Sharingan Energy and reducing the Sharingan Durability of the eye used by 5. The target must make a Wisdom saving throw against your feature save DC. If the target can see you, it makes this saving throw with disadvantage.
If the target makes eye contact with you while within a 30-foot-long, 5-foot-wide line extending from you, and can see or otherwise perceive you, it automatically fails the saving throw.
On a failed save, you gain control over the target for 1 hour. While under your control, the target follows your commands and acts according to your instructions.
If you use this ability against a creature during combat, the target can repeat the Wisdom saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

entries.name: Kotoamatsukami
entries: You can attempt to completely alter a creature's will and beliefs through Kotoamatsukami by expending 50 Sharingan Energy and reducing the Sharingan Durability of the eye used by 25. The target must make a Wisdom saving throw against your feature save DC. If the target can see you, it makes this saving throw with disadvantage.
If the target makes eye contact with you while within a 30-foot-long, 5-foot-wide line extending from you, and can see or otherwise perceive you, it automatically fails the saving throw.

On a failed save, you can permanently rewrite the target's will, beliefs, emotions, and intentions. You can implant new loyalties, create intense hatred toward a creature, or fundamentally alter what the target desires and believes.

For example, you can command a target to become your ally. The target will genuinely regard you as a trusted companion and devote itself to you wholeheartedly. Alternatively, you can make a target develop an intense hatred toward another creature, causing it to relentlessly seek that creature's death.

This ability is not an illusion or ordinary mind control. The target does not realize that its will has been altered and genuinely believes that its new thoughts, feelings, and decisions are its own. The effects are permanent and cannot be ended by repeating the saving throw.
After using this ability, you cannot use Kotoamatsukami: Absolute Control again until a number of years equal to the result of 10d10 have passed.
